title: Election Day scanner problem affects Westchester polling sites - ABC7 New York
text:
Election Day scanner problem affects Westchester polling sites - ABC7 New York 
 24/7 Live New York City New Jersey Long Island Northern Suburbs Connecticut POLITICS 
 Westchester voting machine problems tied to ballot paper issue 
 Jaysha Patel reports from Chappaqua. WABC Tuesday, November 3, 2026 3:29PM Share WESTCHESTER COUNTY, New York (WABC) -- A countywide voting problem that disrupted Election Day operations across Westchester County is being caused by the thickness of paper ballots, according to the Westchester County Board of Elections, which says every ballot cast will still be counted.
 The issue surfaced Tuesday morning when voting machines at polling locations across the county began rejecting ballots. Municipalities, including the Town of North Salem, alerted residents that scanners were not accepting ballots and advised voters to continue casting ballots while election officials worked to resolve the problem.
 The Board of Elections later said the problem involves ballot paper thickness, which is preventing voting machines from accepting ballots at polling places throughout Westchester. Officials said voting remains operational and urged voters not to leave polling locations.
 Election Day live updates: What voters need to know in NY, NJ and CT 
 Voters whose ballots cannot be scanned are being directed to place them in designated orange emergency ballot bags. Election officials said those ballots will remain secure, be monitored and counted in accordance with election procedures.

 The disruption has drawn particular attention because Westchester County is a key battleground in New York's closely watched 17th Congressional District race between Democratic challenger Cait Conley and Republican Rep. Mike Lawler. Both candidates urged voters to stay in line and cast ballots despite the technical issues.
 "There are technical issues with ballot scanners in Westchester, but don't worry: you can still vote and every vote is being counted!" Conley wrote on social media.
 Lawler also sought to reassure voters, saying election officials were working to determine whether the problem stemmed from the ballots or the machines.
 "However, every ballot will be counted. Stay on line and vote. Do not leave the polling place without voting," Lawler said.
 The Board of Elections said it remains in constant communication with New York state officials, county leaders and poll workers as technicians work to restore normal operations. Officials apologized for the disruption and reiterated that voters should not be discouraged from participating.
 "Every eligible vote will be counted. No voter should be discouraged from participating in this election because of this issue," the board said.
